text: The discursive dilemma (List and Pettit) shows that a group deciding each premise by majority vote can be committed to a conclusion that no majority of its members would endorse when voting on the conclusion directly.
explanation: True. This is precisely the discursive dilemma (a generalization of the doctrinal paradox): premise-wise majority voting can yield a collectively endorsed conclusion that conflicts with conclusion-wise majority voting, even when every individual is internally consistent. List and Pettit use it to argue that group attitudes cannot be a simple summative aggregate of individual attitudes, motivating non-summativism about group agency.
